Since 7 July 2025, Epping has stood at the epicentre of national attention, with [http://2025_British_anti-immigration_protests protests and riots erupting over the Government’s use of the Bell Hotel to house asylum seekers]. Demonstrations regularly descended into confrontation, as local residents, anti-fascist campaigners, and far-right activists clashed in scenes unseen in the town for generations.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp8j5vp7413o|title=Epping hotel asylum seeker Hadush Kebatu jailed for sex assaults|date=September 23, 2025|website=BBC News}} The unrest intensified after the sexual assault of a woman and a schoolgirl by a resident of the hotel, whose conviction and sentencing in September 2025 ignited further anger and polarised opinion across the district. In response, the Conservative administration on the council took the unprecedented step of launching a legal challenge against the [[Home Office]], securing a temporary [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] injunction in August 2025 to halt the placement of asylum seekers in the Bell Hotel. That victory proved fleeting: the ruling was overturned at the [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeal]], and the case now stands before the Supreme Court, due for a final judgment in October 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckgy7p29y4ko|title=Epping council given date for The Bell Hotel legal challenge|date=September 16, 2025|website=BBC News}} The crisis has fractured the Conservatives themselves. After months of mounting criticism over their handling of the Bell Hotel unrest, the group lost its majority for the first time since 2006, when two councillors resigned to join the Independents.{{Cite web|url=https://us12.campaign-archive.com/?e=__test_email__&u=40250f17955cfb7586ade94ce&id=f488d7408c|title=EEF NEWS - EXCLUSIVE: Two resignations see Conservatives lose overall control of district council|website=us12.campaign-archive.com}} As a result, the Conservatives will enter the 2026 election defending a fragile minority administration, their dominance of the council for nearly two decades under unprecedented threat. From December 2025 until mid-January, questions surrounded whether the 2026 district elections would proceed as scheduled. In December, the Government invited 63 councils, including Epping Forest, to request a one-year postponement of elections in light of ongoing plans for local government reorganisation, which would replace district, borough and county councils with larger unitary authorities. Following a meeting of the four political group leaders, Epping Forest District Council decided not to seek a delay. As a result, a proposed extraordinary council meeting—at which councillors could have voted on postponement—was cancelled, and the council formally confirmed that the elections would go ahead on 7 May 2026. Council leaders acknowledged concerns that holding elections could delay reorganisation but stated that maintaining democratic accountability took precedence. The decision was publicly welcomed by opposition councillors and the district’s Member of Parliament, [[Neil Hudson (politician)|Dr Neil Hudson]], who argued that residents should retain the right to vote despite the wider structural uncertainty. == Seats up for election == === Close seats === Third place seat where the margin of victory was under 5%: # '''Theydon Bois with Passingford, 0.2% (3 votes)''' # '''Epping West & Rural, 0.9% (17 votes)''' # '''Buckhurst Hill East & Whitebridge, 1.2% (22 votes)''' # '''Rural East, 2.2% (40 votes)''' # '''Waltham Abbey West, 5.1% (66 votes)''' {| class="wikitable" |+ ! === Council ward === ! colspan="2" |Incumbent party !Councillor up for election |- |'''Buckhurst Hill East & Whitebridge''' | {{Party name with colour|Green Party of England and Wales}} |Elizabeth Gabbett |- |'''Buckhurst Hill West''' | {{Party name with colour|Conservative Party (UK)}} |Smruti Patel |- |'''Chigwell with Lambourne''' | {{Party name with colour|Conservative Party (UK)}} |Darshan Sunger |- |'''Epping East''' | {{Party name with colour|Liberal Democrats (UK, 2025)}} |Edward Barnard |- |'''Epping West & Rural''' | {{Party name with colour|Conservative Party (UK)}} |Holly Whitbread |- |'''Grange Hill''' | {{Party name with colour|Conservative Party (UK)}} |Rashni Chahal Holden
